title: Study Permit
desc: A study permit lets you study at a Canadian Designated Learning Institution (DLI).
details: Canada continues to be one of the most popular study destinations, hosting more than 500,000 international students. This is not surprising, given Canada’s world class education system, and the generous benefits provided to students and graduates.
Who Needs a Study Permit?
If you plan to study in Canada at the post-secondary level for 6 months or more, you need to obtain a study permit before your arrival.
The Basic Requirements for a Study Permit
The basic requirements for a Study Permit application are:
A Letter of Acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI) in Canada
Proof of adequate financial support to pay for your tuition and living costs
Police Certificates and a medical examination may be required
Obtaining a Temporary Resident Visa

If you are a national who requires a visa to enter Canada, your study permit application will be combined with a Visitor Visa application (also known as a Temporary Resident Visa or TRV). To receive a Visitor Visa you need to demonstrate strong ties to your home country. This may include documentation that attests to your:
Family ties
Employment ties
Financial ties
Minimum Costs of Studying in Canada

Applicants must demonstrate that they can afford their tuition fees, and afford to live in Canada for the duration of the study period without working. At a minimum, funds covering the first year tuition costs, and first year living costs must be shown.
The requirement is met by showing proof of the funds themselves, and proof of the source of funds.
Tuition fees vary among programs, but most applicants can expect to pay about C$15,000 per year.
The cost of living is set at C$10,000 per year for a single student. $4,000 is added for a second accompanying family member, and an additional $3,000 is added for each additional family member.
Altogether, an applicant needs show show a minimum of C$25,000 ($15,000 for tuition and $10,000 for living costs) in order to be eligible for a study permit.
Accompanying Family Members

Applicants are allowed to bring minor children with them to Canada, and these family members can be included in the application. Unless they are visa exempt, each family member will also need to apply for a Visitor Visa, and if they are of school age, their own Study Permit as well.

Spouses of international students are also able to apply for a Spousal Open Work Permit, which allows them to work full time in Canada for the duration of the study period. The Spousal Open Work Permit can be applied for at the same time as the Study Permit, however in some cases it is recomended that the working spouse apply after studies have begun.
Refused Study Permit Applications

The unfortunate reality is that 30 to 40% of Canadian study permit applications are refused. In some countries, refusal rates climb to 80% or higher.  The good news is that there are option for refused applicants, and in many cases a study permit refusal can be overcome.

title: Express Entry
desc: Immigration programs that allow skilled workers to obtain permanent resident status in Canada based on their economic contribution.
details: What is Express Entry Canada?

Express Entry is the main immigration system used by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) to process permanent residency applications for skilled workers. It is a competitive system, with eligible candidates ranked against one another, based on factors such as age, work experience, education, and language ability. The highest ranking candidates are periodically invited by IRCC to make a permanent residency application. For candidates with competitive profiles, Express Entry is generally the fastest and easiest way to to immigrate to Canada
How do I Qualify for Express Entry Canada?
To qualify for Express Entry, you first need to meet the eligibility requirements for one of the system’s three federal programs:
Federal Skilled Worker Program
The Federal Skilled Worker Program is Canada's largest immigration program which has been in place since 1967. To qualify under this program you must have:
At least 1 year of full-time work experience from the past 10 years, in an occupation listed in the National Occupation Classifcation (NOC) as TEER level 0, 1, 2, or 3.
Good English or French skills (with test results equivalent to a Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB) level of 7)
A score of at least 67 points in the Federal Skilled Worker scoring system
Canadian Experience Class
The Canadian Experience Class is designed for candidates who already have Canadian work experienece. To qualify under this program you must have:
At least one year of full-time Canadian work experience, obtained in the past 3 years, in an occupation listed in the National Occupation Classifcation (NOC) as TEER level 0, 1, 2, or 3.
Good English or French skills (with test results equivalent to a Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB) level of 7 for TEER 0 and 1 occupations, and CLB 5 for TEER 2 and 3 occupations)
Federal Skilled Trades Program
The Federal Skilled Trades Program is designed for candidates with experience in a select list of skilled trades. To qualify under this program you must have:
At least 2 years of full-time work experience in a qualifying skilled trade, within the 5 years before applying
Moderate English or French skills
A valid full-time job offer or a Canadian certiicate of qualification in a skilled trade
What are the Steps to Immigrate with Express Entry?
Immigration to Canada with Express Entry requires the following steps:
Confirm that you meet the requirements for one of the three federal programs: Federal Skilled Worker, Canadian Experience Class, or Federal Skilled Trades.
Take the IELTS, CELPIP, or TEF exam, and if your education is from outside of Canada, obtain an Education Credential Assessment (ECA).
Submit an Express Entry Profile on the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) website, and receive your Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score.
If needed, take steps to increase your CRS score, such as improving your language level, studying in Canada, obtaining a job offer, or obtaining a nomination through the Provincial Nominee Program.
Wait for an Express Entry draw that gives you an Invitation to Apply (ITA) for permanent residence from IRCC. Draws are generally held every 2 or 3 weeks.
Submit your Application for Permanent Residence (APR) to IRCC. You have 60 days from the date of the ITA to electronically submit your application.
How does the Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score work?
After submitting their profile, all Express Entry candidates are given a Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score. The CRS takes into account the following factors:
Age
Level of Education
Proficiency in English and/or French
Foreign and Canadian Work Experience
Canadian Job Offers
Connections to Canada, including Education and Family
Spouse’s Language Proficiency, Education, and Work Experience
Having a Provincial Nomination
IRCC periodically holds Express Entry Draws which select the highest ranking candidates in the pool to receive an Invitation to Apply (ITA) for permanent residence.
How do Express Entry Draws Work?
Express Entry has three different types of draws, also known as Rounds of Invitations:
General Draws: IRCC invites the highest ranking candidates in the entire Express Entry pool
Program-Specific Draws: IRCC invites the highest ranking candidates from a specific program only.
Category-Based Draws: IRCC invites the highest ranking candidates from a specific category, based on certain economic goals set by IRCC
We publish up-to-date details for the Latest Express Entry Draw as well as Express Entry Draw history.
How does the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) work with Express Entry?

In Canada, both the federal and provincial governments are allowed to administer their own immigration programs. The Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) allows Canadian provinces and territories to nominate their own candidates immigration to their region. These nominees then need to be approved for permanent residence by IRCC.

Canadian provinces and territories are able to select candidates from the Express Entry pool  who have declared an interest to live in that province.  A provincial nomination provides the candidate with an additional 600 CRS points, which virtually guarantees an Invitation to Apply (ITA). Given this major boost in points, you do not need to otherwise have a competitive CRS score if you can secure a provincial nomination.
Nonetheless, candidates with the following characteristics will have a major advantage, and may be able to secure an ITA in a general Express-Entry draw without taking further steps:
Under 30 years old
Fluent in English and French
At least three years of skilled work experience
A Master’s level of education

Without this ideal profile success is still possible, but it requires calculated strategy. To increase your CRS score, you may want to consider: retaking your language tests, learning French, obtaining a job offer, or completing a study program in Canada
What Documents are Needed for Express Entry?
After receiving an Invitation to Apply, you have 60 days to submit your permanent residence application. The following documents are required at this time:
Language Test Certificates

You must provide proof of the language test scores that you declared in your Express Entry profile by providing the official test certificates. Eligible tests are: IELTS General Training, CELPIP-General, TEF-Canada, and TCF-Canada. To remain valid, language tests must have been written within 2 years of submitting your application for permanent residence.
Education Documents

You must provide proof of your post-secondary education, including you diplomas, certificates, and transcripts. If you are claiming  CRS points for a non-Canadian program, you must submit your official Education Creential Assessment (ECA) report.
Employment Documents

You must provide proof of all work experience that makes you eligible for your federal immigration program, and for which you are claiming CRS points. For each period of work experience, you need to provide:
Employment Verification Letter, which must:
Be written on company letterhead
Include job title, duties, and responsibilities (to make clear which NOC category the experience falls under)
Include dates for all periods of employment
Include salary and benefits
Include complete contact information for the supervisor/manager/superior who authored the letter
Official Pay Slips
Tax Documentation (if the work period was in Canada, this includes your T4 slip, and your CRA Notice of Assessment)
Police Certificates
You must provide a police certificate from any country where you have lived for 6 months or more, since the age of 18.
What Proof of Funds are Needed for Express Entry?

If you received your Invitation to Apply (ITA) under the Federal Skilled Worker or Federal Skilled Trades programs, you are required to provide proof of funds with your application for permanent residency.  You do not need to provide proof of funds if you received your ITA under the Canadian Experience Class, or if you already are authorised to work in Canada, and have a job offer that meets IRCC's requirements.

IRCC requests proof of funds to ensure that you have sufficient resources to settle in Canada. The required documentation includes letters from the financial institutions that hold your funds, and historical statements for each account. The minimum requirement is based on your family size, including the main applicant, spouse, and any dependent children included in the application. IRCC updates the minimum funds requirements each year.
How long does it take to Immigrate with Express Entry?

Most permanent residency applications submitted through Express Entry are processed by IRCC in six months or less. Individual experiences will vary, however, and processing time following the Invitation to Apply (ITA) can range from as little as two months to up to 24 months.

Since IRCC processing times are calculated from the date the application is submitted following the ITA, you also need to factor in the time it takes to prepare and submit the Express Entry Profile, the time waiting for an ITA, and the preparation time needed following the ITA.
The following factors can influence the time it takes to obtain your permanent residency with Express Entry:
Waiting for the Invitation to Apply

The frequency of Express Entry draws varies, and draw dates are never announced in advance. Even with a competitive CRS score, it can sometimes take weeks or months before there is a draw that you qualify for. Therefore, waiting for an ITA in the Express Entry pool can increase the time it takes to obtain your permanent residency.
Preparing Documents following the Invitation to Apply

You are given 60 days following the ITA to submit your application for permanent residency (APR), and it may take time to gather all documents needed to submit a complete application. Police Certificate processing varies, and for some countries it can take several weeks. It may also take time to receive documentation from past employers. Therefore, if you have not prepared in advance, this stage could add up to two months to the overall time it takes to obtain your permanent residency.
Your Immigration Program
Processing time can vary depending on which of the three federal programs you are applying under, and on whether you also have a nomination under the Provincial Nominee Program.
Biometrics and Medical Examinations

In the early stages of processing, IRCC will invite you to complete your biometrics (submitting your fingerprints and photo at a Visa Application Centre), and to complete your  medical examination. The application will be put on hold until you complete these items. Backlogs at the Visa Application Centres or with the Panel Physicians in your country could lead to delays in scheduling your appointments, which leads to an increase in processing time.
Information Requests During Background Check

In the later stages of processing, IRCC may request additional information, documentation, or forms as part of their background check. This may include requests for additional police certificates, documentation on military service, or clarifications on your work or address history.
Procedural Fairness Letter

If an IRCC officer has doubts about your eligibility under the program you applied for, or has concerns regarding your admissibility to Canada, they may send a Procedural Fairness Letter which gives you an opportunity to respond to the concern. The time it takes to respond to the letter, and the subsequent analysis by the officer, may increase IRCC’s processing time.
How Can I speed Up Express Entry processing?
While you can not directly influence IRCC’s processing times, there are certain things you can do to reduce the possibility for delays in the application process:
Get Ready before the Invitation to Apply

Once you have created your Express Entry Profile, begin the process of requesting your police certificates and collecting employment documentation. This way, you will be ready to submit your Application for Permanent Residency shortly after you get the Invitation to Apply.
Submit a Complete and Thorough Application

The best way to avoid follow up questions from IRCC is to submit a strong application that leaves no doubt about your eligibility, and avoids any additional requests during processing. Make sure that you:

Submit all the necessary police certificates. If you are not sure whether a particular country’s police certificate is needed, submit it anyways to be on the safe side, and to avoid a request later on.
Provide enough employment proof. In addition to employment verification letters and pay slips, also submit third-party proof, such as tax documentation.
Do not have any contradictory information in your application. Make sure the dates of all work history, address history, and past activities are correct.
If there is any aspect of your application which is not typical, provide an explanation letter for the IRCC officer.

title: Post Graduate work-permit
desc: The post-graduation work permit (PGWP) allows students who have graduated from eligible designated learning institutions (DLIs) to gain valuable Canadian work experience.
details: The Post Graduation Work Permit
International students have the opportunity to live and work in Canada following their studies, by receiving a Post Graduation Work Permit (PGWP).
The PGWP is an open work permit which allows the holder to work anywhere in Canada. It is issued once, for a maximum of three years.
The requirements to apply for a PGWP are:
Have successfully completed a full-time study program of at least 8 months, from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI).
You must apply for the PGWP within 180 days of graduation.
If applying in Canada, you must have valid student status at the time of the application.
Qualifying for Permanent Residence
After gaining Canadian work experience or a qualifying job offer, graduates may qualify for Permanent Residence through the Express Entry system, or the Provincial Nominee Program.
Applicants can continue working while their Permanent Residence application is processed by obtaining a Bridging Open Work Permit (BOWP).

title: Visitor Visa
desc:
Visitor Visa Types
Multiple Entry

Multiple entry visas are issued for up to 10 years, or to the expiry date of your passport. You can enter Canada as many times as you want during the validity period. The maximum period of stay for each visit is 6 months from the date of arrival. However, it is possible to extend your legal stay beyond 6 months, by making an application while inside Canada.

Single Entry

Single entry visas allow for a single entry to Canada. 

Visitor Visa Eligibility and Uses
To be eligible for a Visitor Visa, the applicant must:

Prove they have sufficient funds to pay for the visit and return to their home country
Demonstrate sufficient ties to their home country
Be in good health (a medical exam may be required)
Travel/Vacation

Applicants may come to Canada for short or long vacation periods.

Family Visit

Applicants can obtain a visitor visa in order to visit family members. Parents and Grandparents of Canadian citizens or Permanent Residents can also apply for a Super Visa which allows for stays in Canada of up to 2 years at a time.

Business Visit

Applicants may enter for the purpose of business, such as for meetings or conferences. It is important that a visitor visa will not give the holder the right to work - for this a Work Permit is needed.

Short-Term Studies

Applicants who would like to complete a study program of less than 6 months need to obtain a Visitor Visa. For programs of 6 months or more, a Study Permit is also required.

Long-Term Stay

Once inside Canada, a visitor is able to extend their stay beyond 6 months by applying for a Visitor Record. They are also able to apply for a Study Permit, Work Permit, or Permanent Residence, and stay in Canada while the application is processed.
